A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SGV research, with matching authors, core method, and environments. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original trajectory-verification and agent-supervision experiments in Tables 1–4, with additional ablations and benchmark experiments in Appendices D–E.

after.justification: v2 reports original verification, self-refinement, and online-supervision results, plus calibration, robustness, and oracle-validation experiments in its appendices.

M1.justification: The original two-stage SGV algorithm is retained. v2 adds optional implementations using concatenated priors or different models for prior generation (E.8), and integrates verification into a Reflexion loop with persistent reflections (A.2). These extend the inference procedure without replacing its central mechanism.

E1.justification: The three core environments and robotic tool-hang task remain. v2 adds external, human-annotated VisualWebArena trajectories from AgentRewardBench, including BrowserGym execution-error cases (E.1), extending the represented verification data within the existing web domain. VisualWebArena-Lite is the earlier 305-task representative subset renamed, not new task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 substantially expands comparisons with WebJudge, Platt and isotonic calibration, and web-search-grounded verifiers (Tables 10–13 and 20). Its main offline model comparison adds GPT-5, Qwen3, and smaller model variants while dropping GPT-4o and Qwen2.5-VL-72B. Pan et al.'s verifier and the Search Agent/R-MCTS comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v2 changes model versions, replaces universal zero-temperature settings in Table 1 with model-recommended parameters, and revises oracle labels and evaluation rules. OSWorld's main supervision results use verification every five steps instead of only at termination; the documented downstream verifier token limit becomes 8192. New protocols include bias/skewness metrics, calibration trained on 605 trajectories and tested on 305, and a 60-step trajectory-length study.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained two-step and weaker-model ablations, v2 adds extensive tests of scoring templates, calibration, verification frequency, trajectory length, generator–verifier strength, prior diversity, noisy priors, and grounding tools (E.2–E.8). Figure 3 newly quantifies beneficial and harmful intervention outcomes. These substantially broaden the questions tested about reliability and mechanism.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports a bootstrap-estimated percentile threshold in its calibration experiment (E.3.2). Three-run averages for digital environments and 50 robotic rollouts were already documented in v1; there is no stated increase in those counts. Neither version provides systematic confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Many digital results are replaced or added. Online SGV success changes from 50% to 54% in VisualWebArena and from 24.5% to 27% in OSWorld under revised conditions (v1 Table 3; v2 Table 4). New Reflexion results reach 53.9%, versus 46.2% without SGV after three refinements (Figure 2). v1's dedicated GPT-4o results disappear, while robotic results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of trajectories and multimodal verifiers, and the two SGV generation equations, retain their substance. The added formulas concern standard evaluation statistics; the calibration studies are empirical. Neither version supplies new theorems, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The agreement-bias and SGV claims remain, but v2 broadens its advertised contributions to demonstrated self-refinement, verifier-evaluation guidance, and an upgraded benchmark release. It also revises headline performance claims, including a 20-percentage-point advantage over prior VisualWebArena results rather than 16 points. These materially expand the abstract and introduction's contribution scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds an RLHF/sycophancy hypothesis, explains calibration failures through concentrated confidence scores, and discusses the label requirements, domain matching, and cost limiting sampling-based calibration. It also explains trajectory-length results through failure difficulty and examines when periodic intervention helps. These extend the retained discussions of strictness, imperfect oracles, and perceptual limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds Reflexion and scoring-template prompts, calibration fitting and threshold-selection details, prior-generation configurations, and extensive documentation of oracle corrections and environment resets (Appendices A, B, E, F). It also announces model availability alongside code and data. Some reproducibility precision is lost through omitted snapshot identifiers and less explicit model-specific decoding settings.

R1.justification: v2 substantially extends its positioning through new engagement with AgentRewardBench and BrowserGym, RLHF sycophancy, evaluation-template biases, and tool-grounded critique. It uses these connections to distinguish agreement bias, motivate stronger evaluation controls, and position its benchmark repairs. This goes beyond the retained agent, test-time-scaling, and self-bias literature.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and much of the methodological narrative are extensively rewritten. SGV moves from Section 4 into the problem setup, evaluation principles receive a dedicated subsection, and Section 5 expands into downstream applications. Appendices are reorganized around detailed results, ablations, and environment documentation, while substantial earlier material is retained.

P2.justification: v2 redesigns and compresses Figure 1, restructures the main tables with additional metric columns and compact domain summaries, and adds a self-refinement plot, intervention-flow diagrams, response-distribution charts, and numerous analysis tables. Existing qualitative figures are largely retained and relocated. These are substantial display changes beyond numerical updates or renumbering.

improvement.justification: v1 acknowledged unreliable oracles without human-label validation; v2 documents corrections and reports 98% accuracy against external annotations versus 85.1% for the original oracles (Table 9). New calibration, robustness, and self-refinement experiments substantially strengthen the evidence for SGV's mechanism and practical value. Removing the matched-GPT-4o control and introducing reporting inconsistencies, such as Table 15's incompatible sample totals, weaken parts of the revision, but the added validation provides a substantial net improvement.
